comparison.scope: Two fresh, independent three-round batches on the same host. Six samples per target/workload, balanced alternating order across both batches. All samples retained. Frozen production binaries; no builds/tests overlap timers. Existing workload cache preparation is unchanged.
comparison.durability: VaneFS fsync mode: NORMAL immediate per-request transactions and FULL barriers. Drive9 fsync mode: timed fsync waits for remote commit; same pinned local TiDB unistore + MinIO, trust-process-local-events, profile=none. Visibility/caching/persistence boundaries differ; this is a local deployment comparison.
comparison.cache_warning: Upstream hot reads warm the file immediately after fixture fsync. Drive9 can switch from DIRECT_IO to KEEP_CACHE as its two-second bypass expires. The six samples mix actual cache paths; do not describe median ratios as stable storage-read speedups.
comparison.write_timer: create + 1 MiB writes + fsync + close; validation and fixture deletion outside timer. WAL allocation sampled after each application write, not an exact instantaneous peak.
comparison.free_space_policy: Unchanged 1% Drive9 cache guard. Runner requires five GiB above it at batch start and one GiB above it before each sample.

cache_diagnosis.scope: Separate instrumented cache diagnosis, NOT part of timed comparison: unchanged binaries with FUSE debug logs; same 64MiB file read immediately after fsync and after the two-second bypass window.

cache_diagnosis.finding: Drive9 immediate warm open has open_flags=1 (DIRECT_IO); its bypass expires during that read. Next open uses 2 (KEEP_CACHE) and populates pages with 512 FUSE READ requests. After settling, both read passes use 2 and issue zero FUSE READ requests. All four VaneFS passes issue 129 FUSE READ requests. Debug-enabled timings are diagnostic only, not production throughput comparisons.

page_layout.inspection: SQLite dbstat after writer and worker close; inspection uses a separate process from the statically linked SQLite writer.
page_layout.interpretation: 256 MiB split writes allocate 65,792 payload rows (257 MiB of logical 4 KiB blocks, including 256 superseded partial blocks). Payload table occupies about 289.19 MiB because record headers and overflow pages consume space. Version tables and indexes add further pages. All-phase VFS totals include setup, writes, Sync, validation and close; they are not physical device-write counts.

validation.test_scope: No production code changes, so no unrelated test suite rerun. The exact 7cccaf814f production binaries from the previous validated change are frozen and remeasured. New native/FUSE experiments validate contents, SQLite integrity and cleanup.

next_step: Before production changes, prototype larger immutable payload extents inside the existing SQLite transaction boundary. Measure WAL/database bytes and both sequential and 4 KiB random I/O; retain snapshot/branch isolation and atomic rollback. Moving payloads outside SQLite additionally needs an explicit crash-consistency protocol. Do not trade durability or visibility for a benchmark score.
limitations: Shared host with I/O stalls in both targets; all samples are retained. Do not attribute a stall to another process or device behavior from these observations alone.
Changing WAL retention or waiting 20 ms does not reduce VFS WAL bytes. Reducing checkpoint count alone is insufficient to establish throughput improvement.
Read comparisons mix cache states in Drive9. Debug diagnosis confirms possible path transitions, not the exact path taken in every prior uninstrumented sample.
A 256 MiB file and independent three-round batches do not establish long-term throughput in indefinitely growing workspaces.
Native instrumentation adds overhead. Background phases overlap foreground phases and cannot be summed as serial latency. VFS writes are not physical SSD writes.
